explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1089: for n ≥ 2 the limit of g_d(n)/d^{n-1} as d → ∞ exists. g_d(n) is the least m with minimalDistinctDistances(ℝ^d, m) ≥ n, which is the least m such that every m-point set determines at least n distances. This is well defined because the minimum number of distances is monotone in m. The answer yes follows from the two-sided binomial bounds quoted on the page.
